newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First's support dives in TVNZ poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ First's support dives in TVNZ poll.

text.p: Support for New Zealand First Party dived three points to four percent, the lowest in its 3-1/2 year history, according to the latest Television One poll published on Tuesday.
National Party support rose two points to 47 percent, Labour rose one to 32 percent, the Alliance was steady on seven percent as was Act on four percent.
Translated into seats, the coaltion government of National and New Zealand First would have 65 seats, four more than at present.
But NZ First would have just six seats, National 59, Labour 40, Act six and the Alliance nine.
In a question on the preferred prime minister, support for NZ First leader Winston Peters fell two points to four percent, his lowest rating since forming the party.
Peters appears before a Parliament's privileges committee on Wednesday to face charges that he assaulted backbencher John Banks.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger had 28 percent support, while Labour leader Helen Clark rose three points to 22 percent and Alliance leader Jim Anderton rose four to nine percent.
Approval of the coalition government fell six points to 19 percent while disapproval rose 16 points to 65 percent. Sixteen percent of the 1000 polled declined to give an opinion on that question.
